standard.title: Locate and process information in texts
standard.description: locate and process information and ideas in a range of spoken, written and multimodal texts, responding in ways appropriate to cultural context, purpose and audience
standard.prior_knowledge: Students entering at Y7-8 can access and comprehend target language texts in familiar registers from home and community exposure. They can identify key information in known contexts. They have not yet applied systematic information-gathering strategies, evaluated source credibility, or produced structured academic responses to a range of text types.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students locate and process information in a range of spoken, written and multimodal texts — including evaluating sources, responding analytically, and producing structured responses appropriate to cultural context, purpose and audience.

nodes.label: Applying comprehension strategies across text types
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply listening and reading comprehension strategies — note-taking, key fact identification, source evaluation — across a range of target language texts.
nodes.minimum_width: Apply at least two comprehension strategies (e.g. note-taking, key fact identification, main idea extraction) across at least two different text types.
nodes.typical_width: Listen for key facts in spoken texts — phone messages, broadcasts, announcements — using note-taking strategies; access digital and print texts to gather information; evaluate possible sources before undertaking research; read imaginative texts and keep a reading journal.
wider: Evaluate a set of sources for a research task — apply explicit credibility criteria and justify source selection before gathering information
Compare comprehension strategies used in the target language with those used in English academic contexts — identify where the strategies transfer and where they need adaptation
nodes.hinge_reason: Systematic comprehension strategy use is the prerequisite for all information processing and response work. Entry students with strong oral comprehension but limited academic text strategy will struggle to access the full range of text types this descriptor requires.

response_modes.reason: Comprehension strategy repertoire must be built across varied text types — spoken broadcasts, digital texts, imaginative literature, formal documents. Single text type practice produces narrow transfer; varied encounters build flexible strategy use.

success_criteria: Applies at least two comprehension strategies across different text types
Locates key information from at least one spoken and one written text

nodes.label: Accessing and evaluating digital and media texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can access, compare and evaluate digital and media texts in the target language — including using target language search tools and assessing source reliability.
nodes.minimum_width: Access at least two target language digital sources on a topic, evaluate their reliability using at least one explicit criterion, and identify key information from each.
nodes.typical_width: Access digital media in both target language and English to research aspects of Chinese and Australian life; use target language search engines; evaluate source credibility; collate and present information from multiple sources; access social media and traditional texts and express personal opinions.
wider: Conduct a research task using target language search tools and sources — compare the results and perspectives available in target language versus English language sources on the same topic
Evaluate a set of digital sources systematically — categorise them by type, purpose and reliability, and explain which would be most useful for a specific research purpose

response_modes.reason: Digital source evaluation requires explicit criteria and reasoning — students need a framework for assessing reliability, not just an intuitive judgment. Explicit source evaluation instruction followed by guided practice builds systematic assessment capacity.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background language learner entry students may already access target language digital content outside school. Width investment here builds critical evaluation skills on top of existing digital access habits — transforming passive consumption into active, critical information gathering.
success_criteria: Accesses at least two target language digital sources and evaluates reliability using at least one criterion
Identifies key information from each source

nodes.label: Responding analytically and personally to texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can respond to a range of texts with both personal opinion and analytical observation, producing responses appropriate to cultural context, purpose and audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a response to at least one text that includes both a personal opinion and at least one analytical observation about the text's language, purpose or cultural context.
nodes.typical_width: Respond to informative and imaginative texts with personal opinions; view and analyse social media and traditional literary texts; keep a reading journal recording understanding and personal responses; respond to First Nations Australian stories; produce structured responses appropriate to cultural context and audience.
wider: Produce a response to an imaginative text that demonstrates both personal engagement and critical analysis — discussing the cultural context and the author's choices
Compare own response to a text with a peer's — identify where perspectives differ and discuss what personal or cultural background might explain the difference

response_modes.reason: Analytical and personal response integrates comprehension strategy use (node 1) and digital source evaluation (node 2) into a full interpretive act. The teaching investment is in creating genuine response conditions — real texts, real audiences — that require both engagement and critical distance.

success_criteria: Produces a response including both a personal opinion and at least one analytical observation
The response is appropriate to the specified cultural context and audience
